verdict.rationale: Pandoc is fundamentally a programmatic tool. Its first-party docs say it ships both a Haskell library and a standalone command-line program driven entirely by flags and stdin/stdout. It also has an optional HTTP server mode (pandoc-server), so its 'UI' (the CLI) is itself scriptable and there are library and HTTP surfaces. However, no evidence documents that the library or server expose every CLI capability. Server mode is a compile-time option, and the probes found no OpenAPI spec. Missing for 10: documented parity between the CLI and the library/server API, a published API spec for server mode, and independent corroboration of programmatic coverage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Pandoc includes a Haskell library and a standalone command-line program.
server: compile in support for running in HTTP server mode when the executable is renamed (or symlinked as) pandoc-server.
If no input-files are specified, input is read from stdin. Output goes to stdout by default.
